Fresh full ContainerFactory read, both halves including all built-in registrations. Configuration normalization is separate from semantic admission; services populate canonical bases, root definitions are admitted before attachment, typed bootstrap state is wired before extension factories can resolve services. Built-ins and custom extensions finalize once, registries seal, then bootstrap semantic proof is checked. Array extension routing snapshots slots before autoload/owner lookup; service IDs outrank named function fallback. Shared source handlers and explicit Make→Proxy/transformer constraints are intentional. Protected core and canonical binding collisions reject before construction. Constructor/factory autoload cannot ordinarily access the not-yet-exposed container; no hypothetical early-ghost escape is claimed as a bug.

ReferenceDefinition rejects empty entry IDs while preserving any non-empty opaque string including numeric-looking runtime IDs. It remains an argument lookup descriptor rather than a built-in top-level definition strategy; no silent normalization of business IDs.

notes.analysis: BootstrapResolutionGuard records actual semantic usages and winning parameter resolver prefixes, disables recording before finalization, rechecks across revision changes without replaying callbacks, and clears retained uses in finally. A resolver's supports contract and the distinction between previously installed versus newly registered classification are important boundaries; mutable nonconforming extensions must not become artificial production bug claims.

notes.assessment: Attempt-local completed metadata revalidates on registry revision; phase-specific filtering excludes property Proxy before action and includes after metadata-only usages. notes.analysis: ContainerBootstrapState is a one-shot typed handoff with two nullable typed fields written together and read accessors that throw before initialization. OR→AND in duplicate initialization check may be equivalent because no supported state can initialize only one field; requires test anchor rather than a private-state mutant test.

CycleGuard separates local circular resolution from cross-Fiber shared ownership. WeakMap stacks and WeakReference owner tokens avoid keeping abandoned Fibers alive; leaveShared removes ownership only for the current execution and always removes its local stack entry. Main context uses a separate identity token. Empty-stack cleanup and dead-owner handling need contract-level reachability classification, not private map assertions.

DelegatorRegistry snapshots specification before dependency classification, indexes deferred full IDs/owners conservatively, executes ordered callables, and protects resolved-chain cache publication with revisions. Transitive dependency invalidation has queue/visited/entries guards with partially redundant cycle protection; classify each exact survivor against public invalidation semantics and lifetime. deferredDependencies/entryIds only read key sets and do not autoload, rejecting the initial alias-scan reentry hypothesis.

EntryCache supports explicit null values via isset fast path plus array_key_exists, uses independent base/resolved revisions, tracks alias siblings by canonical source, and retains overwritten/removed values into mutation retirement. putBase/putResolved ordinary resolution remain direct. Canonical reverse-index cleanup affects future invalidation precision; direct arbitrary private-cache mutations are not application-level invariants.

ExternalContainerRegistry identity-deduplicates strongly held providers and preserves first-owner order. findOwning snapshots the current batch, then visits only appended suffixes after callbacks/Fiber suspension; earlier has calls are not replayed. Default Container has null registry, avoiding this code path until one is added. No new timing claims or production changes.

MutationRetirement retains roots by reference ownership, sets released and detaches storage before native dropping in insertion order, collects synchronously propagated Throwable causes, and rejects retain after release. Reentrant release is an immediate no-op and no implicit destructor/GC hook exists. Nested graph destructor behavior and later GC exceptions are outside its stated direct-root contract.

notes.assessment: Attempt-local sequence tracks target:index identity and pending attribute object until dispatch; refresh rebuilds at coherent revision, verifies already-executed prefix, never replays handlers; completion guard retains metadata, not resolved entries.

DefinitionBinding captures immutable id/strategy/validated descriptor with private composite ownership token; belongsTo uses identity. Imported snapshots share binding records intentionally while publication accepts only bindings prepared by the destination owner.

Fresh complete validator read: factory admission supports known PHP callable prefixes compatible with (ContainerValue,array), rejects excessive required arguments and internal non-variadic arity below two, uses strict ReflectionType matching with contextual scope and an uninitialized type-only ContainerValue placeholder. Normal container composition protects this factory binding; repeated-lookup mutation affects performance, while invalid foreign-container behavior is an internal defensive surface. Private NUL-key provenance stores only names of mapped string keys, not request values. Membership uses isset and stripping removes all DI-owned metadata via ResolutionMetadata. Normal construction guarantees the private context object; forged private metadata is outside the demonstrated pipeline surface.

Fresh source search found has unused. Wrong-type transport cells are defensive diagnostic behavior, not accepted request objects.
